description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the frequency of external feedback ('o_pop frequency' in units of 10^4) and the accuracy of a language model, showing both initial and final accuracy values. The x-axis, labeled 'o_pop frequency (x10^4)', uses a linear scale ranging from 1 to 19, with tick labels appearing at every integer value. The y-axis, labeled 'Accuracy', uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The plot displays two data series: 'Initial Accuracy', represented by a green line with solid square markers and solid line style, and 'Final Accuracy', represented by a blue line with solid circle markers and solid line style. The green line starts at an accuracy of approximately 0.34 at x=1, dips to a minimum of about 0.3 at x=7, rises to a peak of approximately 0.54 at x=13, and ends at about 0.41 at x=19. The blue line begins at approximately 0.65 at x=1, rises to a peak of about 0.85 at x=9, then declines to a low of around 0.65 at x=13, before rising again to a final value of approximately 0.87 at x=19. Both lines show error bars indicating variability in the measurements.
